targets.name: Create migration, deterministic replay, parity, and performance gates
acceptance: Save migrations and idempotent phase boundaries are tested.
Seeded replay produces stable outcomes across save and resume.
A shared 24- and 72-program test harness checks AI parity, long-horizon balance, and performance.

targets.name: Implement reconciled ledger, cash, obligations, forecast, and runway
acceptance: Every dollar-changing event reconciles to categorized ledger entries and displayed cash.
The player can inspect obligations, runway, and the cause of forecast changes.
Historical statements survive save, resume, and season rollover.

targets.name: Replace fixed tier economics with dynamic core P&L and one operating plan
acceptance: Revenue and expenses resolve from named dynamic components rather than unexplained tier grants.
One preseason operating plan creates visible financial and football tradeoffs.
Winning does not guarantee solvency and money does not directly purchase wins.

targets.name: Prove the core business loop through a deterministic full season
acceptance: A complete season traces operating choices to football capacity, outcomes, audience, revenue, and reinvestment.
Multi-program tests show bounded budgets with no automatic losing-team windfall.
At least three declared operating strategies remain viable in long-horizon seeded tests.

waves.name: Unified command center, position model, and matchup truth

targets.name: Merge the live checklist and scan-first Coach's Desk
acceptance: The dashboard shows no more than three unique unresolved decisions and one dominant next action.
Pending, done, delegated, blocked, required, and optional states update immediately and survive navigation.
At least 90 percent of first-time testers identify the next action and readiness within five seconds.

targets.name: Split defensive backs into CB, FS, and SS
acceptance: New and migrated leagues use CB, FS, and SS with no live DB position while preserving player identity, history, eligibility, ratings, obligations, and scholarship accounting.
Roster generation, depth charts, scheme rotations, ratings, simulation, development, recruiting, portal, training, and AI use one role-specific model under shared rules.
Deterministic 24- and 72-program migration, replay, balance, save/resume, UI, and performance tests prove playable depth and bounded position scarcity.

targets.name: Expose offense, defense, overall, and matchup projections
acceptance: Team ratings derive from actual eligible lineups and scheme usage.
Matchup projections expose favorite or underdog status with scouting-aware uncertainty.
Displayed projections match the resolving simulation inputs and distinguish skill from readiness.

targets.name: Establish shared UI, accessibility, and telemetry contracts
acceptance: Reusable decision, status, comparison, projection, round, and result components cover all defined states.
The core weekly flow passes touch, keyboard, controller, screen-reader, forced-color, zoom, and localization checks.
Telemetry distinguishes impression, expansion, selection, commit, rejection, correction, and advance.

targets.name: Recommend development work by marginal benefit
acceptance: Recommendations rank eligible choices by expected marginal value rather than fragile labels.
The recommendation explains the affected player or room, real projected gain, opportunity cost, and uncertainty.
Deterministic tests cover thin rooms, ceilings, injuries, positional value, and equal-value ties.

targets.name: Pilot staff delegation for depth chart, scouting, and development
acceptance: Manual, recommend, and automatic modes use the same commands, projections, costs, and information boundaries.
Guardrails, named staff attribution, preview, override, and exception escalation are visible and reversible.
Successful delegated work collapses from the attention count while blocked or risky work resurfaces.

targets.name: Unify in-season skill, readiness, potential, and development history
acceptance: Permanent skill, temporary readiness, and potential are mechanically and visually distinct.
Every material rating change has a durable causal record without excessive save growth.
Weekly and offseason growth remain inside declared long-horizon rating distributions.

targets.name: Add the mandatory scan-first season recap phase
acceptance: Season rollover enters recap exactly once before any offseason market or camp.
The default recap communicates verdict, three material outcomes, and next phase within ten seconds.
Financial, football, player, and staff snapshots remain archived and stable across later changes.

waves.name: Shared offseason market and coaching carousel

targets.name: Build one simultaneous multi-round market engine and UI shell
acceptance: Standing offers, portfolios, capacity, simultaneous matching, addressable RNG, movement reports, and save boundaries are shared.
Unchanged terms require no maintenance clicks and inactive rounds skip safely.
Market results are invariant to program iteration and command submission order.

targets.name: Implement contracts, vacancies, and coaching carousel
acceptance: Every coach has a contract term and vacancies require replacement or an explicit interim.
Retention, expiration, firing, poaching, promotion, offers, matching, and cascades use the shared market rules.
Staff continuity affects schemes and players through visible, bounded, deterministic rules.

targets.name: Implement the three-to-five-round portal pursuit
acceptance: Each retained round changes information, leverage, terms, shortlist position, or commitment risk.
Promises, visits, NIL, capacity, withdrawals, and simultaneous commitments remain enforceable and auditable.
Routine portal rounds meet the declared attention and performance budgets for 24- and 72-program leagues.

targets.name: Resolve and show offseason player improvement
acceptance: Camp resolves after carousel, portal, enrollment, and final roster assembly.
Real attribute changes, health effects, team-rating movement, and depth-chart implications are shown separately.
The scan-first result checkpoint cannot duplicate gains and remains calibrated with weekly development.

targets.name: Expand sponsorship, media, donors, capital, debt, and governance
acceptance: Expanded systems post through the common ledger and forecast without creating isolated minigames.
Governance, interventions, recovery, and dismissal respond to declared business objectives and evidence.
AI programs use the same contracts, resources, capital constraints, and consequences.

Kept ARCH-001 in progress for generic weekly planners and system-wide lifecycle adoption.

Verified the ARCH-001 training-camp AI boundary with exact legacy threshold parity, a frozen program-scoped view, hidden-data isolation, exact worker and CLI snapshots, truthful offseason policy attribution, and linked causal events. Kept ARCH-001 in progress for the remaining generic planners and system-wide lifecycle adoption.

Kept ARCH-001 in progress for generic non-weekly AI knowledge completeness and system-wide lifecycle adoption.

Verified the ARCH-001 attributed phase-batch, exact causal event, autosave ordering, controlled delegation, full-season retention, and standing-market outcome slices. Kept ARCH-001 in progress for system-wide AI knowledge boundaries and lifecycle adoption.
